name: Make
tagline: Visual no-code platform for automating workflows between apps.
shortDescription: Visual automation platform (formerly Integromat) for connecting apps and building multi-step workflows.
description: Make, formerly known as Integromat, is a no-code automation platform. You build workflows — called scenarios — on a visual canvas that connects apps and passes data between them.
The visual builder suits workflows with branching, filters and data transformation. It also supports HTTP requests for connecting services without a dedicated integration.
Make has a free plan and paid plans based on usage. Because automation costs scale with how often workflows run, estimate your monthly volume before choosing a plan.

pricing.notes: Pricing is usage-based. Estimate how many operations your workflows will run each month before choosing a plan.

keyFeatures.title: Visual scenario builder
keyFeatures.description: Design workflows on a canvas and see how data flows between steps.

keyFeatures.title: App integrations
keyFeatures.description: Connect a large library of apps. Check the official site for a specific app.

keyFeatures.title: Routers and filters
keyFeatures.description: Branch workflows and add conditions for more complex logic.

keyFeatures.title: HTTP and webhooks
keyFeatures.description: Connect services via APIs and webhooks when there is no ready-made integration.

howItWorks: Create an account and start a new scenario.
Add a trigger, such as a new form submission or a scheduled time.
Add actions in other apps and map data between them.
Test the scenario with sample data, then switch it on.
useCases: Sending form leads to a CRM and email list
Syncing data between spreadsheets and apps
notIdealFor: Someone who wants the simplest possible two-step automations
pros: Visual builder makes complex logic easier to follow
Supports generic HTTP requests and webhooks
cons: Usage-based pricing needs estimating up front
Visual logic has a learning curve for beginners

checklist: Time for a beginner to build a three-step workflow (form → spreadsheet → email)
Error handling and retry behaviour when a connected app fails
Free plan operations allowance on the date of testing
Availability of integrations for a list of 20 common apps

faqs.q: Is Make the same as Integromat?
faqs.a: Yes. Integromat was rebranded as Make.

faqs.q: Make or Zapier — which should I use?
faqs.a: It depends on your workflows and budget. Read our Make vs Zapier comparison for the key differences.
